items.title: Activity: First Capture
items.desc:
Learning goal:
Get comfortable opening Wireshark, starting a capture, and recognizing that the "network" is actually a stream of readable, identifiable traffic, not a black box.
Materials needed:
* Laptop
* Wireshark installed (pre-class requirement)

items.title: Activity: Delay-Calculation Problem Set
items.desc: Compute processing, queueing, transmission, and propagation delay separately, and recognize which one dominates in different scenarios.

items.title: Activity: Traceroute Lab
items.desc:
Use traceroute to see the actual path traffic takes, and connect hop-by-hop delay jumps to bottleneck links from the pre-class video.
* Pick 3 destinations.
* Run traceroute to each:
* Mac/Linux: traceroute example.com
* Windows: tracert example.com
* For each destination, record the delay at every hop.
* Graph hop number (X-axis) vs. delay (Y-axis) for all three destinations, on the same chart if possible.
* Which destination had the steepest delay increase, and at which hop?

items.title: Lab 1
items.desc:

* Add a getter for each field.
* Add a setter for at least one field, and make it actually validate, reject a bad value rather than blindly assigning it (e.g. reject a negative quantity, an empty name, whatever makes sense for your class).
